+ // @vitest-environment jsdom
+ import { cleanup, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react'
+ import { createElement } from 'react'
+ import { afterEach, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
+ import ThreadCard from '../src/renderer/src/components/ThreadCard'
+ import ThreadView from '../src/renderer/src/views/ThreadView'
+ import { useCrew, type ThreadMeta } from '../src/renderer/src/state/store'
+ import type { SessionEvent } from '../src/shared/events'
+ 
+ class TestResizeObserver {
+   observe(): void {}
+   unobserve(): void {}
+   disconnect(): void {}
+ }
+ 
+ global.ResizeObserver = TestResizeObserver as unknown as typeof ResizeObserver
+ 
+ const thread = (voice: boolean): ThreadMeta => ({
+   id: 't1',
+   agentId: 'a1',
+   agentLabel: 'Fable',
+   title: 'what broke',
+   createdBy: 'ALI',
+   status: 'open',
+   mode: 'build',
+   voice
+ })
+ 
+ const said = (id: string, text: string, voice?: boolean): SessionEvent => ({
+   id,
+   ts: 1,
+   kind: 'message',
+   authorId: 'ali',
+   authorName: 'ALI',
+   text,
+   mentions: [],
+   threadId: 't1',
+   voice
+ })
+ 
+ const load = (voice: boolean, events: SessionEvent[]) => {
+   useCrew.setState({
+     connection: 'online',
+     selfId: 'ali',
+     selfName: 'ALI',
+     members: [{ id: 'ali', name: 'ALI', connected: true }],
+     agents: [
+       {
+         id: 'a1',
+         label: 'Fable',
+         provider: 'claude',
+         ownerId: 'ali',
+         ownerName: 'ALI',
+         status: 'idle',
+         runs: {},
+         settings: {},
+         fields: []
+       }
+     ],
+     events,
+     docs: {},
+     threads: { t1: thread(voice) },
+     threadPrompts: {},
+     threadDrafts: {},
+     chatDraft: '',
+     chatCommands: [],
+     queues: {},
+     steps: {},
+     tokens: {},
+     pending: {},
+     openThreadId: 't1',
+     docsTarget: null
+   })
+ }
+ 
+ const card = (voice: boolean) => {
+   load(voice, [])
+   render(
+     createElement(ThreadCard, {
+       thread: thread(voice),
+       ts: 1,
+       state: 'ready' as const,
+       detail: '',
+       onOpen: () => {}
+     })
+   )
+ }
+ 
+ describe('a thread somebody spoke says so', () => {
+   afterEach(cleanup)
+ 
+   it('wears the Voice chip on its card the way a plan wears its own', () => {
+     card(true)
+     expect(screen.getByText('Voice')).toBeTruthy()
+   })
+ 
+   it('says nothing on the card of a thread somebody typed', () => {
+     card(false)
+     expect(screen.queryByText('Voice')).toBeNull()
+   })
+ 
+   it('marks the line that was said rather than the box it was typed in', () => {
+     load(true, [said('m1', 'what broke', true), said('m2', 'and this one I typed')])
+     render(createElement(ThreadView, { threadId: 't1' }))
+ 
+     const marks = screen.getAllByText('Spoken')
+     expect(marks).toHaveLength(1)
+     const row = marks[0].parentElement as HTMLElement
+     const stamp = row.querySelector('span[class*="text-fg-faint"]') as HTMLElement
+     expect(stamp).toBeTruthy()
+     expect(stamp.compareDocumentPosition(marks[0]) & Node.DOCUMENT_POSITION_FOLLOWING).toBeTruthy()
+     expect(row.textContent).toContain('ALI')
+   })
+ 
+   it('leaves the composer header alone', () => {
+     load(true, [said('m1', 'what broke', true)])
+     render(createElement(ThreadView, { threadId: 't1' }))
+ 
+     const header = screen.getByLabelText('Back to chat').closest('div') as HTMLElement
+     expect(header.textContent).not.toContain('Spoken')
+   })
+ })
+

step.text:
All four tests are passing. Let me verify that the "leaves the composer header alone" test is actually catching what I expect — when I call `closest('div')` from the back button, it traverses up through the Tooltip span wrapper and lands on the header row div with the flex styling. The test would have failed before my change if the header still had the pill styling, so this confirms the fix is working correctly.

Now I need to run the other test suites I modified: threads.integration, thread-mentions, ghost.integration since the server chat path changed, and possibly chat-log. The server change routes commands through the thread branch, but commands inside threads are still ignored for mode, so I should run ghost, threads, and plan tests to be safe.

I see that `voice-check` runs in Node rather than the browser, so it can't actually test the WebGPU path—it just hardcodes the dtype instead of pulling from `models.ts`. I need to update the plan so `voice-check` reads the wasm settings from `models.ts` to keep that fallback path covered, while noting that the WebGPU path can only be tested in the actual app. Now I'm laying out the file-by-file order, starting with Phase 1 to remove the waits.

First, I'll add a `voice` flag to the prompt message in the protocol. Then both places in `session.ts` that send prompt messages need to include that flag based on whether the thread has voice enabled. In `runner/index.ts`, the `runPrompt` function takes this flag and skips the `onBeforeRun` hook for spoken turns, though the sync loop still runs every 5 seconds so edits still propagate. The key piece is `models.ts` needs a `backend()` function that returns device and dtype settings—WebGPU when available (with fp32 for Kokoro and fp16/q4 for Whisper), otherwise the current wasm settings. Finally, both worker files need to load through this backend function and gracefully fall back to wasm if the WebGPU load or first inference fails, plus set the thread count from hardware concurrency.

For the SharedArrayBuffer piece, I'm considering whether to enable it in Electron via the command-line flag in `src/main/index.ts`—it would unlock multithreaded wasm without needing CSP changes or headers, and Electron does support this flag natively.

For warming up the voice models, I'd add a `warm()` function in `src/renderer/src/state/voice.ts` that runs once when a session starts, wrapped in `requestIdleCallback`. The tricky part is that kokoro would produce audio during warmup, so I'd have the worker discard that output while Whisper warms up on silent input.

Now I'm thinking about the next phase around turn boundaries, specifically adding a `pausing` state to the gate logic... The first release of a turn might end mid-clause—at a comma, colon, or semicolon—so I need to wait until at least ~16 characters are safe before releasing, then handle everything after that as sentence-granular chunks like today. The `grew` method already knows whether it's the first release through `this.at === 0`. For barge-in and reuse, `findTurn` should follow the message rather than the prompt text, locating the `message` event this window sent and then its `message.route` to get the promptId for both queued and steered turns.

I need to track whether a turn was steered, and when a reply is adopted mid-run, it should start from the text already on screen rather than re-reading from the beginning. The turn-end grace period becomes a configurable number passed to the provider instead of a constant—spoken turns get a longer grace (around 20 seconds) so the second turn in a conversation can steer into a live CLI without spawning a new process and rebuilding the transcript. The steer path already exists in the session layer, so nothing new is needed there.

For the narration phase, I'm creating a new module that maps steps to spoken lines by reading the tool actions. Narration reads from the first thinking step's opening line if there's been silence for a couple seconds. I'm also setting up tests for the voice system—covering listening with the new gate word, reply handling with clause rules, turn-finding through message routing, mouth behavior with asides and barge-ins, a new test for narration steps converting to lines, and an integration test to verify spoken prompts carry voice context to the runner.

The `yarn voice-check` command should pull the dtype from `models.ts` instead of hardcoding it, and WebGPU visibility is limited to the app itself. I'm considering adding a timing readout behind a dev flag—maybe a console line that logs each turn's four spans in dev builds so tuning happens against actual numbers rather than intuition. Skipping the sync for voice is the biggest win with the smallest code change, so that should come first in the priority order.

On the tradeoff of skipping sync: the AGENTS.md rule exists because agents on different machines need to see the same code before acting, so a spoken turn would run against whatever's currently on disk. The 5-second loop still commits and pushes the result, though, so on a single-machine crew there's no practical difference. I'll be explicit about that tradeoff.

Now I'm writing this up with section headers for each phase, backticks around file paths, and rough budget estimates labeled clearly. I need to avoid em dashes and semicolons used as dashes.
